doc.brief: Iterates over the contents of a `GtkTextBuffer`.
doc.md:
Iterates over the contents of a `GtkTextBuffer`.

You may wish to begin by reading the
[text widget conceptual overview](section-text-widget.html),
which gives an overview of all the objects and data types
related to the text widget and how they work together.

assign.md:
Assigns the value of `other` to `iter`.

This function is not useful in applications, because
iterators can be assigned with `GtkTextIter i = j;`.

The function is used by language bindings.

backward_char.brief: Moves backward by one character offset.
backward_char.md:
Moves backward by one character offset.

Returns `TRUE` if movement was possible; if `iter` was the first
in the buffer (character offset 0), this function returns `FALSE`
for convenience when writing loops.

backward_chars.md:
Moves `count` characters backward, if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer, moves
to the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the iterator moved
onto a dereferenceable position; if the iterator didn’t move, or
moved onto the end iterator, then `FALSE` is returned. If `count` is 0,
the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`.

backward_cursor_positions.md:
Moves up to `count` cursor positions.

See [`TextIter.forward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_cursor_position) for details.

backward_find_char.brief: Same as [`TextIter.forward_find_char()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_find_char), but goes backward from `iter`.
backward_find_char.md:
Same as [`TextIter.forward_find_char()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_find_char),
but goes backward from `iter`.

backward_line.brief: Moves `iter` to the start of the previous line.
backward_line.md:
Moves `iter` to the start of the previous line.

Returns `TRUE` if `iter` could be moved; i.e. if `iter` was at
character offset 0, this function returns `FALSE`. Therefore,
if `iter` was already on line 0, but not at the start of the line,
`iter` is snapped to the start of the line and the function returns
`TRUE`. (Note that this implies that
in a loop calling this function, the line number may not change on
every iteration, if your first iteration is on line 0.)

backward_lines.md:
Moves `count` lines backward, if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer, moves to
the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the iterator moved
onto a dereferenceable position; if the iterator didn’t move, or
moved onto the end iterator, then `FALSE` is returned. If `count` is 0,
the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`. If `count` is negative,
moves forward by 0 - `count` lines.

backward_search.md:
Same as [`TextIter.forward_search()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_search), but moves backward.

`match_end` will never be set to a `GtkTextIter` located after `iter`,
even if there is a possible `match_start` before or at `iter`.

backward_sentence_start.brief: Moves backward to the previous sentence start.
backward_sentence_start.md:
Moves backward to the previous sentence start.

If `iter` is already at the start of a sentence, moves backward
to the next one.

Sentence boundaries are determined by Pango and should
be correct for nearly any language.

backward_sentence_starts.md:
Calls [`TextIter.backward_sentence_start()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:backward_sentence_start) up to `count` times.

If `count` is negative, moves forward instead of backward.

backward_to_tag_toggle.brief: Moves backward to the next toggle (on or off) of the `tag`, or to the next toggle of any tag if `tag` is `NULL`.
backward_to_tag_toggle.md:
Moves backward to the next toggle (on or off) of the
`tag`, or to the next toggle of any tag if
`tag` is `NULL`.

If no matching tag toggles are found,
returns `FALSE`, otherwise `TRUE`. Does not return toggles
located at `iter`, only toggles before `iter`. Sets `iter`
to the location of the toggle, or the start of the buffer
if no toggle is found.

backward_visible_cursor_position.brief: Moves `iter` backward to the previous visible cursor position.
backward_visible_cursor_position.md:
Moves `iter` backward to the previous visible cursor position.

See [`TextIter.backward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:backward_cursor_position) for details.

backward_visible_cursor_positions.brief: Moves up to `count` visible cursor positions.
backward_visible_cursor_positions.md:
Moves up to `count` visible cursor positions.

See [`TextIter.backward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:backward_cursor_position) for details.

backward_visible_line.brief: Moves `iter` to the start of the previous visible line.
backward_visible_line.md:
Moves `iter` to the start of the previous visible line.

Returns `TRUE` if
`iter` could be moved; i.e. if `iter` was at character offset 0, this
function returns `FALSE`. Therefore if `iter` was already on line 0,
but not at the start of the line, `iter` is snapped to the start of
the line and the function returns `TRUE`. (Note that this implies that
in a loop calling this function, the line number may not change on
every iteration, if your first iteration is on line 0.)

backward_visible_lines.brief: Moves `count` visible lines backward, if possible.
backward_visible_lines.md:
Moves `count` visible lines backward, if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer, moves to
the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the iterator moved
onto a dereferenceable position; if the iterator didn’t move, or
moved onto the end iterator, then `FALSE` is returned. If `count` is 0,
the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`. If `count` is negative,
moves forward by 0 - `count` lines.

backward_visible_word_start.brief: Moves backward to the previous visible word start.
backward_visible_word_start.md:
Moves backward to the previous visible word start.

If `iter` is currently on a word start, moves backward to the
next one after that.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

backward_word_start.brief: Moves backward to the previous word start.
backward_word_start.md:
Moves backward to the previous word start.

If `iter` is currently on a word start, moves backward to the
next one after that.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language

can_insert.brief: Considering the default editability of the buffer, and tags that affect editability, determines whether text inserted at `iter` would be editable.
can_insert.md:
Considering the default editability of the buffer, and tags that
affect editability, determines whether text inserted at `iter` would
be editable.

If text inserted at `iter` would be editable then the
user should be allowed to insert text at `iter`.
[`TextBuffer.insert_interactive()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:insert_interactive) uses this function
to decide whether insertions are allowed at a given position.

compare.brief: A qsort()-style function that returns negative if `lhs` is less than `rhs`, positive if `lhs` is greater than `rhs`, and 0 if they’re equal.
compare.md:
A qsort()-style function that returns negative if `lhs` is less than
`rhs`, positive if `lhs` is greater than `rhs`, and 0 if they’re equal.

Ordering is in character offset order, i.e. the first character
in the buffer is less than the second character in the buffer.

copy.brief: Creates a dynamically-allocated copy of an iterator.
copy.md:
Creates a dynamically-allocated copy of an iterator.

This function is not useful in applications, because
iterators can be copied with a simple assignment
(`GtkTextIter i = j;`).

The function is used by language bindings.

editable.brief: Returns whether the character at `iter` is within an editable region of text.
editable.md:
Returns whether the character at `iter` is within an editable region
of text.

Non-editable text is “locked” and can’t be changed by the
user via `GtkTextView`. If no tags applied to this text affect
editability, `default_setting` will be returned.

You don’t want to use this function to decide whether text can be
inserted at `iter`, because for insertion you don’t want to know
whether the char at `iter` is inside an editable range, you want to
know whether a new character inserted at `iter` would be inside an
editable range. Use [`TextIter.can_insert()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:can_insert) to handle this
case.

ends_line.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `iter` points to the start of the paragraph delimiter characters for a line.
ends_line.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `iter` points to the start of the paragraph
delimiter characters for a line.

Delimiters will be either a newline, a carriage return, a carriage
return followed by a newline, or a Unicode paragraph separator
character.

Note that an iterator pointing to the \n of a \r\n pair will not be
counted as the end of a line, the line ends before the \r. The end
iterator is considered to be at the end of a line, even though there
are no paragraph delimiter chars there.

ends_sentence.md:
Determines whether `iter` ends a sentence.

Sentence boundaries are determined by Pango and should
be correct for nearly any language.

ends_tag.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `tag` is toggled off at exactly this point.
ends_tag.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `tag` is toggled off at exactly this point.

If `tag` is `NULL`, returns `TRUE` if any tag is toggled off at this point.

Note that if this function returns `TRUE`, it means that
`iter` is at the end of the tagged range, but that the character
at `iter` is outside the tagged range. In other words,
unlike [`TextIter.starts_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:starts_tag), if this function
returns `TRUE`, [`TextIter.has_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:has_tag) will return
`FALSE` for the same parameters.

ends_word.brief: Determines whether `iter` ends a natural-language word.
ends_word.md:
Determines whether `iter` ends a natural-language word.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

equal.brief: Tests whether two iterators are equal, using the fastest possible mechanism.
equal.md:
Tests whether two iterators are equal, using the fastest possible
mechanism.

This function is very fast; you can expect it to perform
better than e.g. getting the character offset for each
iterator and comparing the offsets yourself. Also, it’s a
bit faster than [`TextIter.compare()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:compare).

forward_char.brief: Moves `iter` forward by one character offset.
forward_char.md:
Moves `iter` forward by one character offset.

Note that images embedded in the buffer occupy 1 character slot, so
this function may actually move onto an image instead of a character,
if you have images in your buffer. If `iter` is the end iterator or
one character before it, `iter` will now point at the end iterator,
and this function returns `FALSE` for convenience when writing loops.

forward_chars.md:
Moves `count` characters if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer,
moves to the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the new position of
`iter` is different from its original position, and dereferenceable
(the last iterator in the buffer is not dereferenceable). If `count`
is 0, the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`.

forward_cursor_position.brief: Moves `iter` forward by a single cursor position.
forward_cursor_position.md:
Moves `iter` forward by a single cursor position.

Cursor positions are (unsurprisingly) positions where the
cursor can appear. Perhaps surprisingly, there may not be
a cursor position between all characters. The most common
example for European languages would be a carriage return/newline
sequence.

For some Unicode characters, the equivalent of say the letter “a”
with an accent mark will be represented as two characters, first
the letter then a "combining mark" that causes the accent to be
rendered; so the cursor can’t go between those two characters.

See also the [`LogAttr`](xref:gtk:Pango.LogAttr) struct and the `break`
function.

forward_cursor_positions.md:
Moves up to `count` cursor positions.

See [`TextIter.forward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_cursor_position) for details.

forward_find_char.md:
Advances `iter`, calling `pred` on each character.

If `pred` returns `TRUE`, returns `TRUE` and stops scanning.
If `pred` never returns `TRUE`, `iter` is set to `limit` if
`limit` is non-`NULL`, otherwise to the end iterator.

forward_line.brief: Moves `iter` to the start of the next line.
forward_line.md:
Moves `iter` to the start of the next line.

If the iter is already on the last line of the buffer,
moves the iter to the end of the current line. If after
the operation, the iter is at the end of the buffer and not
dereferenceable, returns `FALSE`. Otherwise, returns `TRUE`.

forward_lines.md:
Moves `count` lines forward, if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer, moves to
the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the iterator moved
onto a dereferenceable position; if the iterator didn’t move, or
moved onto the end iterator, then `FALSE` is returned. If `count` is 0,
the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`. If `count` is negative,
moves backward by 0 - `count` lines.

forward_search.md:
Searches forward for `str`.

Any match is returned by setting `match_start` to the first character
of the match and `match_end` to the first character after the match.
The search will not continue past `limit`. Note that a search is a
linear or O(n) operation, so you may wish to use `limit` to avoid
locking up your UI on large buffers.

`match_start` will never be set to a `GtkTextIter` located before `iter`,
even if there is a possible `match_end` after or at `iter`.

forward_sentence_end.brief: Moves forward to the next sentence end.
forward_sentence_end.md:
Moves forward to the next sentence end.

If `iter` is at the end of a sentence, moves to the next
end of sentence.

Sentence boundaries are determined by Pango and should
be correct for nearly any language.

forward_sentence_ends.md:
Calls [`TextIter.forward_sentence_end()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_sentence_end) `count` times.

If `count` is negative, moves backward instead of forward.

forward_to_end.brief: Moves `iter` forward to the “end iterator”, which points one past the last valid character in the buffer.
forward_to_end.md:
Moves `iter` forward to the “end iterator”, which points
one past the last valid character in the buffer.

[`TextIter.get_char()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_char) called on the end iterator
returns 0, which is convenient for writing loops.

forward_to_line_end.brief: Moves the iterator to point to the paragraph delimiter characters.
forward_to_line_end.md:
Moves the iterator to point to the paragraph delimiter characters.

The possible characters are either a newline, a carriage return,
a carriage return/newline in sequence, or the Unicode paragraph
separator character.

If the iterator is already at the paragraph delimiter
characters, moves to the paragraph delimiter characters for the
next line. If `iter` is on the last line in the buffer, which does
not end in paragraph delimiters, moves to the end iterator (end of
the last line), and returns `FALSE`.

forward_to_tag_toggle.brief: Moves forward to the next toggle (on or off) of the `tag`, or to the next toggle of any tag if `tag` is `NULL`.
forward_to_tag_toggle.md:
Moves forward to the next toggle (on or off) of the
`tag`, or to the next toggle of any tag if
`tag` is `NULL`.

If no matching tag toggles are found,
returns `FALSE`, otherwise `TRUE`. Does not return toggles
located at `iter`, only toggles after `iter`. Sets `iter` to
the location of the toggle, or to the end of the buffer
if no toggle is found.

forward_visible_cursor_position.brief: Moves `iter` forward to the next visible cursor position.
forward_visible_cursor_position.md:
Moves `iter` forward to the next visible cursor position.

See [`TextIter.forward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_cursor_position) for details.

forward_visible_cursor_positions.brief: Moves up to `count` visible cursor positions.
forward_visible_cursor_positions.md:
Moves up to `count` visible cursor positions.

See [`TextIter.forward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_cursor_position) for details.

forward_visible_line.brief: Moves `iter` to the start of the next visible line.
forward_visible_line.md:
Moves `iter` to the start of the next visible line.

Returns `TRUE` if there
was a next line to move to, and `FALSE` if `iter` was simply moved to
the end of the buffer and is now not dereferenceable, or if `iter` was
already at the end of the buffer.

forward_visible_lines.brief: Moves `count` visible lines forward, if possible.
forward_visible_lines.md:
Moves `count` visible lines forward, if possible.

If `count` would move past the start or end of the buffer, moves to
the start or end of the buffer.

The return value indicates whether the iterator moved
onto a dereferenceable position; if the iterator didn’t move, or
moved onto the end iterator, then `FALSE` is returned. If `count` is 0,
the function does nothing and returns `FALSE`. If `count` is negative,
moves backward by 0 - `count` lines.

forward_visible_word_end.brief: Moves forward to the next visible word end.
forward_visible_word_end.md:
Moves forward to the next visible word end.

If `iter` is currently on a word end, moves forward to the
next one after that.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language

forward_word_end.brief: Moves forward to the next word end.
forward_word_end.md:
Moves forward to the next word end.

If `iter` is currently on a word end, moves forward to the
next one after that.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

free.brief: Free an iterator allocated on the heap.
free.md:
Free an iterator allocated on the heap.

This function is intended for use in language bindings,
and is not especially useful for applications, because
iterators can simply be allocated on the stack.

get_buffer.brief: Returns the `GtkTextBuffer` this iterator is associated with.
get_buffer.md: Returns the `GtkTextBuffer` this iterator is associated with.

get_bytes_in_line.brief: Returns the number of bytes in the line containing `iter`, including the paragraph delimiters.
get_bytes_in_line.md:
Returns the number of bytes in the line containing `iter`,
including the paragraph delimiters.

get_char.brief: The Unicode character at this iterator is returned.
get_char.md:
The Unicode character at this iterator is returned.

Equivalent to operator* on a C++ iterator. If the element at
this iterator is a non-character element, such as an image
embedded in the buffer, the Unicode “unknown” character 0xFFFC
is returned. If invoked on the end iterator, zero is returned;
zero is not a valid Unicode character.

So you can write a loop which ends when this function returns 0.

get_chars_in_line.brief: Returns the number of characters in the line containing `iter`, including the paragraph delimiters.
get_chars_in_line.md:
Returns the number of characters in the line containing `iter`,
including the paragraph delimiters.

get_child_anchor.brief: If the location at `iter` contains a child anchor, the anchor is returned.
get_child_anchor.md:
If the location at `iter` contains a child anchor, the
anchor is returned.

Otherwise, `NULL` is returned.

get_language.brief: Returns the language in effect at `iter`.
get_language.md:
Returns the language in effect at `iter`.

If no tags affecting language apply to `iter`, the return
value is identical to that of `get_default_language`.

get_line.brief: Returns the line number containing the iterator.
get_line.md:
Returns the line number containing the iterator.

Lines in a `GtkTextBuffer` are numbered beginning
with 0 for the first line in the buffer.

get_line_index.brief: Returns the byte index of the iterator, counting from the start of a newline-terminated line.
get_line_index.md:
Returns the byte index of the iterator, counting
from the start of a newline-terminated line.

Remember that `GtkTextBuffer` encodes text in
UTF-8, and that characters can require a variable
number of bytes to represent.

get_line_offset.brief: Returns the character offset of the iterator, counting from the start of a newline-terminated line.
get_line_offset.md:
Returns the character offset of the iterator,
counting from the start of a newline-terminated line.

The first character on the line has offset 0.

get_marks.brief: Returns a list of all `GtkTextMark` at this location.
get_marks.md:
Returns a list of all `GtkTextMark` at this location.

Because marks are not iterable (they don’t take up any "space"
in the buffer, they are just marks in between iterable locations),
multiple marks can exist in the same place.

The returned list is not in any meaningful order.

get_offset.brief: Returns the character offset of an iterator.
get_offset.md:
Returns the character offset of an iterator.

Each character in a `GtkTextBuffer` has an offset,
starting with 0 for the first character in the buffer.
Use [`TextBuffer.get_iter_at_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:get_iter_at_offset) to convert
an offset back into an iterator.

get_paintable.brief: If the element at `iter` is a paintable, the paintable is returned.
get_paintable.md:
If the element at `iter` is a paintable, the paintable is returned.

Otherwise, `NULL` is returned.

get_slice.brief: Returns the text in the given range.
get_slice.md:
Returns the text in the given range.

A “slice” is an array of characters encoded in UTF-8 format,
including the Unicode “unknown” character 0xFFFC for iterable
non-character elements in the buffer, such as images.
Because images are encoded in the slice, byte and
character offsets in the returned array will correspond to byte
offsets in the text buffer. Note that 0xFFFC can occur in normal
text as well, so it is not a reliable indicator that a paintable or
widget is in the buffer.

get_tags.brief: Returns a list of tags that apply to `iter`, in ascending order of priority.
get_tags.md:
Returns a list of tags that apply to `iter`, in ascending order of
priority.

The highest-priority tags are last.

The `GtkTextTag`s in the list don’t have a reference added,
but you have to free the list itself.

get_text.brief: Returns text in the given range.
get_text.md:
Returns text in the given range.

If the range
contains non-text elements such as images, the character and byte
offsets in the returned string will not correspond to character and
byte offsets in the buffer. If you want offsets to correspond, see
[`TextIter.get_slice()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_slice).

get_toggled_tags.brief: Returns a list of `GtkTextTag` that are toggled on or off at this point.
get_toggled_tags.md:
Returns a list of `GtkTextTag` that are toggled on or off at this
point.

If `toggled_on` is `TRUE`, the list contains tags that are
toggled on. If a tag is toggled on at `iter`, then some non-empty
range of characters following `iter` has that tag applied to it.  If
a tag is toggled off, then some non-empty range following `iter`
does not have the tag applied to it.

get_visible_line_index.brief: Returns the number of bytes from the start of the line to the given `iter`, not counting bytes that are invisible due to tags with the “invisible” flag toggled on.
get_visible_line_index.md:
Returns the number of bytes from the start of the
line to the given `iter`, not counting bytes that
are invisible due to tags with the “invisible” flag
toggled on.

get_visible_line_offset.brief: Returns the offset in characters from the start of the line to the given `iter`, not counting characters that are invisible due to tags with the “invisible” flag toggled on.
get_visible_line_offset.md:
Returns the offset in characters from the start of the
line to the given `iter`, not counting characters that
are invisible due to tags with the “invisible” flag
toggled on.

get_visible_slice.brief: Returns visible text in the given range.
get_visible_slice.md:
Returns visible text in the given range.

Like [`TextIter.get_slice()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_slice), but invisible text
is not included. Invisible text is usually invisible because
a `GtkTextTag` with the “invisible” attribute turned on has
been applied to it.

get_visible_text.brief: Returns visible text in the given range.
get_visible_text.md:
Returns visible text in the given range.

Like [`TextIter.get_text()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_text), but invisible text
is not included. Invisible text is usually invisible because
a `GtkTextTag` with the “invisible” attribute turned on has
been applied to it.

has_tag.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `iter` points to a character that is part of a range tagged with `tag`.
has_tag.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `iter` points to a character that is part
of a range tagged with `tag`.

See also [`TextIter.starts_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:starts_tag) and
[`TextIter.ends_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:ends_tag).

in_range.brief: Checks whether `iter` falls in the range [`start`, `end`).
in_range.md:
Checks whether `iter` falls in the range [`start`, `end`).

`start` and `end` must be in ascending order.

inside_sentence.brief: Determines whether `iter` is inside a sentence (as opposed to in between two sentences, e.g. after a period and before the first letter of the next sentence).
inside_sentence.md:
Determines whether `iter` is inside a sentence (as opposed to in
between two sentences, e.g. after a period and before the first
letter of the next sentence).

Sentence boundaries are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

inside_word.brief: Determines whether the character pointed by `iter` is part of a natural-language word (as opposed to say inside some whitespace).
inside_word.md:
Determines whether the character pointed by `iter` is part of a
natural-language word (as opposed to say inside some whitespace).

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

Note that if [`TextIter.starts_word()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:starts_word) returns `TRUE`,
then this function returns `TRUE` too, since `iter` points to
the first character of the word.

is_cursor_position.brief: Determine if `iter` is at a cursor position.
is_cursor_position.md:
Determine if `iter` is at a cursor position.

See [`TextIter.forward_cursor_position()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:forward_cursor_position) or
[`LogAttr`](xref:gtk:Pango.LogAttr) or `break` for details
on what a cursor position is.

is_end.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `iter` is the end iterator.
is_end.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `iter` is the end iterator.

This means it is one past the last dereferenceable iterator
in the buffer. [`TextIter.is_end()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:is_end) is the most efficient
way to check whether an iterator is the end iterator.

is_start.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `iter` is the first iterator in the buffer.
is_start.md: Returns `TRUE` if `iter` is the first iterator in the buffer.

order.brief: Swaps the value of `first` and `second` if `second` comes before `first` in the buffer.
order.md:
Swaps the value of `first` and `second` if `second` comes before
`first` in the buffer.

That is, ensures that `first` and `second` are in sequence.
Most text buffer functions that take a range call this
automatically on your behalf, so there’s no real reason to
call it yourself in those cases. There are some exceptions,
such as [`TextIter.in_range()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:in_range), that expect a
pre-sorted range.

set_line.brief: Moves iterator `iter` to the start of the line `line_number`.
set_line.md:
Moves iterator `iter` to the start of the line `line_number`.

If `line_number` is negative or larger than or equal to the number of lines
in the buffer, moves `iter` to the start of the last line in the buffer.

set_line_index.brief: Same as [`TextIter.set_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_offset), but works with a byte index.
set_line_index.md:
Same as [`TextIter.set_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_offset), but works with a
byte index. The given byte index must be at
the start of a character, it can’t be in the middle of a UTF-8
encoded character.

set_line_offset.brief: Moves `iter` within a line, to a new character (not byte) offset.
set_line_offset.md:
Moves `iter` within a line, to a new character (not byte) offset.

The given character offset must be less than or equal to the number
of characters in the line; if equal, `iter` moves to the start of the
next line. See [`TextIter.set_line_index()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_index) if you have a byte
index rather than a character offset.

set_offset.md:
Sets `iter` to point to `char_offset`.

`char_offset` counts from the start
of the entire text buffer, starting with 0.

set_visible_line_index.brief: Like [`TextIter.set_line_index()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_index), but the index is in visible bytes, i.e. text with a tag making it invisible is not counted in the index.
set_visible_line_index.md:
Like [`TextIter.set_line_index()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_index), but the index is in visible
bytes, i.e. text with a tag making it invisible is not counted
in the index.

set_visible_line_offset.brief: Like [`TextIter.set_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_offset), but the offset is in visible characters, i.e. text with a tag making it invisible is not counted in the offset.
set_visible_line_offset.md:
Like [`TextIter.set_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:set_line_offset), but the offset is in visible
characters, i.e. text with a tag making it invisible is not
counted in the offset.

starts_line.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `iter` begins a paragraph.

This is the case if [`TextIter.get_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_line_offset)
would return 0. However this function is potentially more
efficient than [`TextIter.get_line_offset()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:get_line_offset), because
it doesn’t have to compute the offset, it just has to see
whether it’s 0.

starts_sentence.md:
Determines whether `iter` begins a sentence.

Sentence boundaries are determined by Pango and
should be correct for nearly any language.

starts_tag.brief: Returns `TRUE` if `tag` is toggled on at exactly this point.
starts_tag.md:
Returns `TRUE` if `tag` is toggled on at exactly this point.

If `tag` is `NULL`, returns `TRUE` if any tag is toggled on at this point.

Note that if this function returns `TRUE`, it means that
`iter` is at the beginning of the tagged range, and that the
character at `iter` is inside the tagged range. In other
words, unlike [`TextIter.ends_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:ends_tag), if
this function returns `TRUE`, [`TextIter.has_tag()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextIter#method:has_tag)
will also return `TRUE` for the same parameters.

starts_word.brief: Determines whether `iter` begins a natural-language word.
starts_word.md:
Determines whether `iter` begins a natural-language word.

Word breaks are determined by Pango and should be correct
for nearly any language.

toggles_tag.brief: Gets whether a range with `tag` applied to it begins or ends at `iter`.
toggles_tag.md:
Gets whether a range with `tag` applied to it begins
or ends at `iter`.

This is equivalent to (gtk_text_iter_starts_tag() ||
gtk_text_iter_ends_tag())
